Package org.aeonbits.owner.formats.json

package org.aeonbits.owner.formats.json
Reads a configuration written in JSON - a source whose path ends in .json - flattening it into the keys the rest of the library already speaks: server.host, servers[0].host.

The parser is JsonParser, written here rather than taken from a library, which is what lets owner-formats be added to a build without adding anything else. It is small because the type is declared by the mapping interface and not by the file: a scalar is kept as the text it was written with and converted where every other value is converted.

Three questions a JSON document can ask that a properties file cannot, answered the same way whenever they come up: a null writes no key at all, so a Config.DefaultValue covers it; an empty array writes an empty value; and a name repeated inside one object is refused rather than resolved, since the two readings of it - the last one wins, or a list - are both somebody's expectation.
